extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent prosecutors, and patent practitioners (applicants and attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria for determining patent term adjustment (PTA) and reductions under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and implementing regulations (37 CFR 1.702-1.705), including what delays count for adjustment, what applicant actions reduce adjustment, and applicability/effective-date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bases for patent term adjustment (37 CFR 1.702)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is entitled to patent term adjustment if the Office fails to perform certain acts of examination within specified time frames (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(A)) and for other delays specified in 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(B) and (C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.702 sets forth the bases for PTA and applies to utility and plant applications filed on or after May 29, 2000. Effective-date variations exist; Office personnel must consider which regulatory version applies to a particular application or patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to original applications (37 CFR 1.702(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 37 CFR 1.702-1.705 apply only to original (i.e., non-reissue) applications, except design patent applications, filed on or after May 29, 2000, and patents issued on such applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued prosecution applications (CPAs) filed on or after May 29, 2000 may be entitled to PTA; a request for continued examination (RCE) under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) is not a new application and filing an RCE in an application filed before May 29, 2000 does not cause entitlement to PTA. International-applications must have an international filing date on or after May 29, 2000 to be covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment — failure to mail notification/notice within 14 months (37 CFR 1.703(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The period beginning the day after the date that is fourteen months after filing (or national-stage commencement) and ending on the date of mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first, counts toward adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications granted on or after January 14, 2013 the 14-month measurement is from filing under 111(a) or national-stage commencement under 371(b)/(f). For some pre-2013 cases, measurement for international applications is based on the date the application fulfilled 371 requirements rather than national-stage commencement. See effective-date notes in 37 CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment — interference or derivation proceedings (37 CFR 1.703(a)(2), 1.702(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Days between institution of an interference or derivation proceeding involving the application and the date that the proceeding was terminated with respect to the application; and days prosecution was suspended due to other interferences/derivation proceedings, count toward adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective Sept. 16, 2012, derivation proceedings were added (AIA changes). Both proceedings instituted involving the application and suspensions due to proceedings not involving the application can generate adjustment days, to the extent periods do not overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment — secrecy orders (37 CFR 1.703(a)(3), 1.702(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Days the application was maintained in sealed condition under 35 U.S.C. 181, days from mailing of an examiner's answer under § 41.39 while under secrecy until secrecy removal, and days from applicant notification that a proceeding would be instituted but for the secrecy order until secrecy removal, count toward adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy-order related delays are explicitly included in adjustment calculations; specific start/end events are the dates of sealing, examiner's answer, notification, and removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment — applicant appellate/appeal-related delays (37 CFR 1.703(a)(4) & (5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Days beginning four months after filing an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 (or four months after filing a reply in compliance with § 1.113(c) or similar adjustments) and ending on mailing of examiner's answer under § 41.39, an action under 35 U.S.C. 132, or a notice of allowance; also days four months after a final decision by the PTAB or federal court (if at least one allowable claim remains) until mailing of an action or notice of allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four-month delayed-start periods are used to compute the portion of adjustment attributable to appeal practice or appellate decisions. Effective-date amendments (AIA) changed references to PTAB and added derivation proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment — post-issue-fee delay (37 CFR 1.703(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Days beginning the day after the date that is four months after payment of the issue fee and satisfaction of outstanding requirements and ending on the date a patent was issued count toward adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This captures Office delay occurring after the applicant has paid the issue fee and completed requirements; the start is four months after that date and stops at patent issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year delay rule and its measurement (37 CFR 1.703(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The period beginning the day after the date that is three years after filing (or national-stage commencement for international apps) and ending on the date a patent was issued counts toward adjustment, except that certain periods are excluded (see specified exclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-year measurement recognizes long Office prosecution delays; international-applications use national-stage commencement rules as defined. Various exclusions (RCEs, applicant delays, PTAB jurisdiction, etc.) are listed in paragraphs (b)(1)-(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — time consumed by a request for continued examination (RCE) (37 CFR 1.703(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Time consumed by continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) is excluded from the three-year period: specifically, the period beginning on the date an RCE was filed and ending on the date of mailing of the notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective January 9, 2015 this interpretation is clarified to apply to patents granted before, on, or after that date. See Novartis AG v. Lee for related jurisprudence and MPEP § 2731 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — periods when jurisdiction is with PTAB or in appeal (37 CFR 1.703(b)(4) and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Days beginning when jurisdiction passes to the PTAB under § 41.35(a) and ending when PTAB jurisdiction ends under § 41.35(b), or ending on the date of the last federal court decision in appeal under 35 U.S.C. 141 or civil actions under 145, are excluded from the three-year delay calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective-date rule changes and AIA redesignation to PTAB are reflected; for notices of allowance after Sept. 17, 2012, different exclusions may apply per amended regulation text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summation, overlap, and limits on adjustment (37 CFR 1.703(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustment equals the sum of periods calculated under paragraphs (a)–(e) to the extent not overlapping, but shall not exceed the actual number of days the issuance of the patent was delayed; the term is adjusted by the sum of the periods less the sum of periods under § 1.704.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When periods overlap they are not double-counted; certificates of mailing/transmission dates under § 1.8 are not taken into account. The final adjustment cannot exceed actual days of delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: No adjustment beyond a filed disclaimer date (37 CFR 1.703(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: No patent whose term has been disclaimed beyond a specified date shall be adjusted under § 1.702 and § 1.703 beyond the expiration date specified in the disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A terminal disclaimer that shortens the patent term limits any PTA to not extend beyond the disclaimer date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for applicant failure to engage in reasonable efforts (37 CFR 1.704(a),(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment shall be reduced by periods during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution (processing or examination) of the application. In particular, cumulative reply times in excess of three months to any Office notice/action count as applicant delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the three-month period from the date the Office communication was mailed; the shortened statutory period for reply set in an Office action or notice does not affect the three-month measurement. The reduction applies with respect to PTA grounds, especially the three-year ground in § 1.702(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-requested suspension of action (37 CFR 1.704(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution is suspended under § 1.103 at the applicant’s request, the period of adjustment is reduced by the number of days between the date the request for suspension was filed and the date the suspension terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspensions initiated by applicant reduce PTA for the corresponding calendar days; overlapping periods handled per 1.703(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of issuance at applicant's request (37 CFR 1.704(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If issuance of a patent is deferred under § 1.314 at the applicant’s request, the adjustment is reduced by the number of days between the date a deferral request was filed and the date the patent was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant-requested deferrals are treated as applicant delay, reducing PTA by the deferral duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment or late payment of issue fee (37 CFR 1.704(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application was abandoned or the issue fee was paid late, the period of adjustment is reduced by days beginning on the date of abandonment or the date after the issue fee was due and ending on the earlier of (i) mailing of decision reviving the application or accepting late issue fee payment, or (ii) four months after filing a grantable petition to revive or accept late payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This captures applicant-caused interruptions in prosecution due to abandonment or late payment; reduction is limited to the earlier of revival decision or four months after a grantable petition was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file petition to withdraw abandonment or to revive within two months (37 CFR 1.704(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment or to revive is not filed within two months of the mailing date of a notice of abandonment, the adjustment is reduced by days beginning the day after the two-month deadline and ending on the date the petition is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant inaction after notice of abandonment beyond the two-month window counts as delay reducing PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of provisional to nonprovisional (37 CFR 1.704(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: When converting a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(b) to a nonprovisional under 111(a) per 111(b)(5), PTA is reduced by days beginning on the date the application was filed under 111(b) and ending on the date a compliant request to convert per § 1.53(c)(3) was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays attributable to conversion timing are treated as applicant delay and reduce PTA accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment or paper filed less than one month before Office action/notice requiring supplemental action (37 CFR 1.704(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a preliminary amendment or other preliminary paper is filed less than one month before mailing of an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 that requires a supplemental Office action or notice, the reduction is the lesser of (i) days between the original mailing date and the supplemental mailing date, or (ii) four months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This penalizes last-minute applicant submissions that trigger additional Office work close to mailing dates; the reduction is capped at four months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply having an omission (37 CFR 1.704(c)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply contains an omission under § 1.135(c), the period of adjustment is reduced by days beginning the day after the omitted reply was filed and ending on the date the correcting reply or paper was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections to incomplete replies are treated as applicant delay for PTA reduction purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reply or other paper after reply (not requested) (37 CFR 1.704(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a supplemental reply or other paper (other than one expressly requested by the examiner) after a reply has been filed results in reduction by days beginning the day after the initial reply and ending on the date the supplemental reply or paper was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsolicited follow-up papers that prolong prosecution timeline count as applicant-caused delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment or paper after PTAB or federal court decision filed less than one month before Office action/notice requiring supplement (37 CFR 1.704(c)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment or paper (other than those tied to new grounds under § 41.50(b)/(c)) after a PTAB decision or federal court decision and less than one month before mailing of an Office action or notice that requires a supplemental mailing will reduce PTA by the lesser of (i) days between original mailing and supplemental mailing, or (ii) four months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors the preliminary-amendment rule for amendments filed after appellate decisions that force extra Office work shortly before a mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment under § 1.312 or other paper filed after notice of allowance (37 CFR 1.704(c)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment under § 1.312 or other paper (other than an RCE under § 1.114) after a notice of allowance was given or mailed reduces PTA by the lesser of (i) days between filing the amendment/paper and the mailing date of the Office action or notice in response, or (ii) four months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant-initiated post-allowance filings that cause extra Office work shorten PTA up to four months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 within three months (37 CFR 1.704(c)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 is not filed within three months from the date a notice of appeal to the PTAB was filed under 35 U.S.C. 134 and § 41.31, PTA is reduced by days beginning day after that three-month deadline and ending when an appeal brief complying with § 41.37 or a request for continued examination under § 1.114 is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late appeal briefs or substituting an RCE count as applicant delay reducing PTA; measure from the notice-of-appeal filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing an RCE after a notice of allowance (37 CFR 1.704(c)(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) filed after a notice of allowance has been mailed results in PTA reduction by days beginning the day after mailing of the notice of allowance and ending on the date the RCE was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an RCE post-allowance is treated as applicant-caused delay and reduces PTA for the interval between allowance mailing and the RCE filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to provide application in condition for examination within eight months (37 CFR 1.704(c)(13))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is not in condition for examination as defined in paragraph (f) within eight months from filing (or national-stage commencement), PTA is reduced by days beginning the day after the eight-month date and ending on the date the application is in condition for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must supply required elements (specification with at least one claim and abstract, compliant papers/drawings/sequence listings, oath/declaration or ADS with required info, and required fees) within eight months or face PTA reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further prosecution via continuing application (37 CFR 1.704(c)(14))
rubrics_metrics.description: When further prosecution occurs via a continuing application, the period of adjustment shall not include any period that is prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time spent in prior parent applications before the filing date of the patent-applying application is not included in PTA for the later patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS-only filings and timing exception (37 CFR 1.704(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper containing only an information disclosure statement (IDS) in compliance with §§ 1.97 and 1.98, or an RCE that contains only an IDS, will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts under certain paragraphs if accompanied by a statement certifying that each item was first cited in a communication from a patent office and that the communication was not received by any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than thirty days prior to filing the IDS (or the communication meets the same timing requirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thirty-day period for this exception is not extendable. This protects applicants from PTA reductions for IDS filings triggered by newly-received foreign or Office communications received within 30 days before filing the IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request under § 1.705(c) for reinstatement of reduced PTA not treated as failure (37 CFR 1.704(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a request under § 1.705(c) for reinstatement of reduced patent term adjustment will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution under paragraph (c)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing for reinstatement of reduced PTA per § 1.705(c) is exempt from being itself characterized as applicant delay for the specified paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for examination — what must be present (37 CFR 1.704(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is in condition for examination when it includes a specification (including at least one claim and an abstract), papers in compliance with § 1.52, drawings if any in compliance with § 1.84, any required English translation, sequence listings if applicable in compliance with §§ 1.821–1.825, the inventor's oath/declaration or an application data sheet containing § 1.63(b) information, the basic filing fee (§ 1.16(a) or (c)), the search fee (§ 1.16(k) or (m)), the examination fee (§ 1.16(o) or (q)), any required certified copy of a previous application, and any application size fee required under § 1.16(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications, condition for examination is entering the national stage as defined in § 1.491(b) and meeting analogous requirements and fee payments under § 1.492. Correcting papers/drawings/sequence listings before the date of mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance will be considered for purposes of being in condition for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective-date and AIA-related amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Various regulatory paragraphs include effective-date dependent text (e.g., amendments applicable to patents issued on or after Jan. 14, 2013; amendments applicable only to notices of allowance mailed on or after Sept. 17, 2012; changes effective Jan. 9, 2015; and changes relating to Dec. 18, 2013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office personnel and practitioners must apply the correct regulatory version based on filing dates, notice-of-allowance dates, and patent-grant dates; the MPEP notes where alternative regulatory texts apply and cites relevant Federal Register notices.
